narrative_purpose: Shows the countercurrent trick of a fish gill: blood flowing opposite to water keeps the oxygen gradient open along the whole exchange surface.
subject: A flat schematic of a single gill frond. A horizontal blood vessel runs across the middle, with an arrow pointing left-to-right. Above it, a band of water flow with an arrow pointing right-to-left (the opposite way). Between the two, a row of short vertical arrows showing oxygen crossing downward from the water into the blood, spaced evenly along the entire length, all roughly the same strength end to end - signalling the gradient never dies.
scene: Empty dark space background, only the two opposed flow bands and the small crossing arrows between them.
camera: Flat head-on schematic view, no perspective, no 3D.
light: Flat even lighting; the flow bands and arrows glow on their own.
palette: Near-black background, cyan band for the water flow, magenta band for the blood flow, small teal crossing arrows between them.
style: Clean elegant infographic of thin glowing lines and arrows, like a vector schematic.
detail_level: Two clearly opposed flow arrows, an even row of small crossing arrows between them, generous space; nothing cluttered.
composition: Two long horizontal bands one above the other with opposite-pointing arrows, evenly spaced small vertical arrows in the gap between.
consistency_notes: Thin glowing cyan/magenta/teal shapes on a near-black background; the shared visual language for every schematic diagram in this chapter.
negative_prompt: no text, no letters, no numbers, no busy clutter, no photorealism, no 3D bevels, no drop shadows
